finding: Community-based Chicago sample: CFS cases subclassified by symptom frequency showed differences in sociodemographics and disability.
Vignette study: a medical-sounding label (CNDS) led PAs to rate the syndrome as more severe than 'CFS'.

During 3-stage tilt, MCA blood flow velocity did not differ from controls at baseline or in response; NMH 21 vs 14 (p=.22) and POTS 9 vs 7 (p=.76) did not differ, though symptom onset was earlier in CFS.
note: Transcranial Doppler velocity not flow; small; ET-CO2 measured

finding: Veterinary 'CFS-like' disease in pets; not human ME/CFS.
Occupational therapy assessment/intervention framework with a case study.
SPECT at rest and during PASAT: diffuse regional cerebral blood flow pattern and less anterior cingulate perfusion in CFS, with equal task performance.
CFS patients had lower plasma/LDL vitamin E and lag phase and higher LDL TBARS, correlating with fatigue and lower muscle pain thresholds.
Conceptual paper applying the Model of Human Occupation to CFS.
In a randomized double-blind crossover, cognitive decrements followed perceived (not actual) chemical exposure.

population: CFS-like illness in Gulf War veterans
finding: Gulf War veterans had higher CFS-like illness (adjusted OR 4.8) and PTSD (OR 3.1) than non-Gulf veterans.
Immunobead assay for ciguatoxin-like 'chronic phase lipids' was positive (titer >=1:40) in 95.6% of 115 CFS sera vs few normals.
note: Non-standard assay, not replicated, specificity unclear

finding: Plasma bacterial 16S rDNA was found less often in CFS (14%) than controls (32%, p=0.03); no unique bacterial sequences in CFS.

n: 21 CFS vs 24 non-CFS fatigue vs 44 syncope vs 21 healthy
finding: Abnormal tilt endpoints occurred in 79% of CFS vs 35% non-CFS chronic fatigue, 46% syncope and 14% healthy; hemodynamic instability score OR 34.8 vs healthy.
Haemochromatosis prevalence in 88 CFS patients (2.3%) was not above population levels.
CFS had lower function and more fatigue than MS; somatic attributions, illness worry and depression related to disability.
Systematic review of literature on disability in CFS (no abstract available).
Hypothesis paper proposing conditioned amygdala sympathetic output as a CFS mechanism.
CFS patients showed distinct defense patterns and more retrospectively reported negative life events than healthy controls.
Russian patent for physical-therapy method.
Patent claiming SNRIs for CFS/fibromyalgia.
Antioxidants reduced immobility and normalised brain oxidative markers in a mouse forced-swim model labelled CFS.
note: Animal model of despair, not validated for ME/CFS

finding: Blood PCR detected Mycoplasma species in 68.6% of European CFS patients vs 5.6% of controls.
note: PCR-only, single group, not independently replicated

finding: CFS patients had lower baseline ACTH and lower ACTH responses to psychosocial stress, exercise and insulin tolerance test, with no difference in total plasma cortisol responses.
Patent for dopamine agonists in fibromyalgia and CFS.
Patent on detoxification-gene genotyping to predict chemical-induced disease.
After multidisciplinary treatment, post-infectious CFS improved (8 of 9 back to work) and NK activity rose; non-infectious CFS did not (3 of 9).
NK cell activity was suppressed in both post-infectious and non-infectious CFS groups.
Women with surgically diagnosed endometriosis reported higher rates of CFS, fibromyalgia, hypothyroidism and autoimmune disease than the general US female population.
Commentary on the UK Chief Medical Officer's CFS/ME working group report.
Secondary analysis of a psychological-treatment RCT: poor outcome was predicted by self-help group membership, sickness benefit and dysphoria.
note: Interpretation of predictors as 'secondary gain' is speculative

finding: CFS reported lower overt self-esteem than both comparison groups.
1H-MRS showed a higher occipital choline/creatine ratio in CFS (0.97 vs 0.76, p=0.008) with no other metabolite differences.
After a maximal treadmill test, CFS patients' rest-activity circadian period lengthened beyond 24 h while controls' did not.
Patients at immunology and psychiatry fatigue clinics were similar in symptoms, disability and distress, but more immunology attenders attributed illness to physical causes (64% vs 31%).
In CFS of under 2 years' duration, 46% self-reported improvement at 1 year; complete recovery occurred only with duration under 15 months.
Birth order showed a non-significant tendency toward more second-born children in gradual-onset CFS.

Tilt evoked postural tachycardia or presyncope in only a minority of CFS patients; supine HR was higher (66.4 vs 57.4 bpm) and stroke volume fell markedly in tilt-negative patients, suggested as deconditioning.
IL-6 infusion raised somatic symptoms faster in CFS than controls but did not impair cognition in either group.
Fatigued twins had substantial SF-36 impairment (especially physical function) versus unaffected co-twins at all case-definition levels.
ANA prevalence, including nuclear-envelope ANA, did not differ between CFS, Gulf War illness and controls.

n: 23 CFS vs 77 comparison (FMF, psoriatic arthritis, anxiety, syncope, healthy)
finding: A fractal/recurrence score of heart rate and pulse transit time during short tilt separated CFS from controls with 70% sensitivity and 88% specificity.
note: Derived and tested in same sample, no validation

finding: Serology and PCR for HHV-6/7/8, CMV, EBV, HSV, VZV, parvovirus B19 and others did not differ between twins with CFS and healthy co-twins.
High-dose clonidine challenge raised growth hormone (p=0.028) and cortisol (p=0.021) more in CFS than controls, suggesting supersensitive central alpha-2 receptors.
note: Small; challenge test, not a treatment trial

finding: The 37-kDa RNase L fragment in CFS PBMC extracts is a proteolytic product (elastase-like) of native RNase L that remains 2-5A-dependent and active.
note: Biochemistry; sample size not in abstract

finding: Latent class analysis of 32 symptoms gave four graded classes, supporting CFS and fibromyalgia as more similar than different.
CFS/FM patients reported more daily hassles, distress, fatigue, pain, depression and anxiety than MS/RA patients.
PBMC beta-endorphin was lower in CFS and fibromyalgia than in healthy controls or depressed patients.
Narrative review of psychiatric comorbidity, HPA dysregulation and treatment of CFS; notes a subgroup with basal hypocortisolaemia.
Lack of physician legitimisation (36%) was associated with higher depression and anxiety scores in CFS.
A fatigue version of the Tampa kinesiophobia scale (beliefs about activity) explained about 12% of variance in walking distance in CFS.
Development and validation of the 12-item FibroFatigue observer rating scale.
In a follow-up questionnaire after an inpatient multidisciplinary programme, 78% of responding adolescents attended school full-time or nearly so up to 5 years later.
CFS patients showed no objective cognitive impairment versus controls, though they rated their own cognition lower.
CFS patients had more fatigue, functional impairment, pain and lower activity (actometer) than severely fatigued breast cancer survivors.
Nasal lavage TNF-alpha, IL-8, NGF and total protein did not differ between CFS and non-CFS subjects.
HCMV IgM antibodies to nonstructural proteins p52 and CM2 were found in a subset of 16 CFS patients but not in 77 controls.
Internet CFS treatment information agreed with systematic reviews only 4-68% of the time.
The 37-kDa RNase L in CFS PBMC is structurally related to the native 80-kDa enzyme (shared N-terminus and peptides), complexed with RNase L inhibitor, and not made by alternative splicing.
note: Biochemistry; sample size not in abstract

finding: After acute B19 infection, followed patients had more arthralgia and fatigue than controls; CFS may follow B19 but attribution without acute serology is difficult.
CFS patients had normal salivary cortisol profiles but enhanced, prolonged suppression after 0.5 mg dexamethasone.
Interviews with carers of CFS patients described coping and acceptance as resignation over time.
Narrative review of fibromyalgia and myalgic encephalomyelopathy, proposing a new pain-disorder paradigm.
Hypothesis that omega-3 supplements could treat CFS by lowering IL-1 and TNF production.
Private body consciousness and somatic symptom report were related to slower reaction-time information processing in CFS.
Of 73 CFS patients, 46 had elevated RNase L; this group had lower peak VO2 and exercise duration than the normal-RNase L group.
note: No healthy control group; RNase L assay not widely replicated

finding: Lymphocyte surface markers and NK activity showed more variability in discordant twins but no significant CFS-specific difference (CD62L+ T cells higher, not significant).
Medical trainees viewed CFS as serious, but the name 'myalgic encephalopathy' was regarded as more serious than 'CFS'.
About half of CFS patients showed delayed-type hypersensitivity to Candida antigens, correlating with in vitro T-cell activation and urinary neopterin kinetics.
note: No controls in abstract; unusual assay

finding: Fukuda symptoms (headache, sore throat, lymph node and joint pain, muscle pain) differentiated CFS from controls but not melancholic depression from controls.
Women reported stigma mainly before diagnosis, including doubt and psychologising of symptoms.
Family-focused CBT was followed by improvement in 15 of 18 adolescents at 6 months.
Patent claiming antivirals for CFS as persistent herpesvirus infection.
Sociological thesis on illegitimacy and stigma of ME/CFS.
Actual Stroop performance did not differ after depression correction, but patients consistently underestimated their performance.
Physicians recognised psychiatric disorder in 64% of CFS patients who had one, indicating under-recognition.
Parent and child negative illness beliefs were related, and negative beliefs about consequences related to symptom-focused coping.
PBMC array of 1764 genes separated most CFS cases from controls, with 8 differentially expressed genes (including IL-8, CMRF35).
Antioxidants reduced immobility and normalised brain oxidative markers in a mouse swim model labelled CFS.
Allergen-specific IgE positivity in 50 CFS patients (36%) was not different from the general population, arguing against an atopy link.

n: 16 M + 17 F vs matched sedentary controls
finding: VO2max was not different in male CFS (40.5 vs 43.3 mL/kg/min) and 4 mL/kg/min lower in female CFS (30.0 vs 34.2, p=0.002), with both groups near age-predicted values (96-101%).
CFS patients had slower reaction times on all four measures of a computerised and a telephone version of the CDR cognitive battery.

population: ME/CFS (CFS, civilians and Gulf War veterans)
finding: Cytokine (Th2) and lymphocyte factors predicted CFS status and function in Gulf War veterans but not civilians, and reaction time mediated the effect.
note: Factor analysis; n not in abstract

finding: Neural-network-derived symptom classification criteria separated CFS from SLE and FM with 95% sensitivity and 85% specificity.
86% of respondents wanted a name change, with patients and physicians split between 'myalgic encephalopathy' and 'neuro-endocrine immune disorder'.

n: 25 CFS vs 37 healthy, 30 FM, 15 GAD, 20 hypertension
finding: A tilt-test hemodynamic instability score based on BP and HR variability separated CFS from healthy controls and other patient groups.
note: Derived and tested in same sample

finding: At 5 years, 68% of the CBT group vs 36% of the relaxation group rated themselves much improved, with more complete recovery and work hours, though few reached normal fatigue levels.
RNase L and PKR antiviral pathway gene expression was upregulated in acute infection but not in CFS, so activation is unlikely to serve as a CFS diagnostic.
note: Gene expression, not enzyme fragment assay

finding: CFS patients interpreted symptoms as physical illness more than depressed or normal groups, and least as negative emotion.
CFS and controls did not differ on intellectual functioning and memory but differed in suggestibility and automatic processing.
CFS veterans had cognitive deficits on 3 of 8 computerised measures after adjusting for premorbid AFQT scores.
Ten CFS patients with active HHV-6A infection followed 24 months had slightly raised HHV-6 DNA copies, increased lymphocyte apoptosis and variable CD4/CD8 ratios.
note: No controls; selected for active HHV-6

finding: 46% of CFS patients had a defensive high-anxious coping style versus fewer in comparison groups (p=0.012).
In a community sample, childhood abuse predicted idiopathic and psychiatric fatigue but not CFS.
Patients with CFS and fibromyalgia and their significant others both scored high on premorbid 'action-proneness'.
LPS-stimulated whole-blood IL-10 was higher in CFS and more sensitive to dexamethasone suppression.
Review on defining and managing CFS (no abstract available).
First-degree relatives of CFS cases had higher rates of CFS than relatives of controls, without greater familial depression loading.
Systematic review of 44 controlled trials of CFS interventions found heterogeneous outcomes (38 measures) across 12 to 326 participants per trial.
note: Qualitative synthesis; conclusions truncated in abstract

finding: Peak cardiovascular and ventilatory values were lower in CFS, with the main difference a lower heart rate at equal relative and maximal workloads.
TMS corticospinal inhibition was normal in CFS (duration and extent not different from controls).
In a Brussels fatigue clinic cohort, Fukuda and Holmes definitions could be separated by symptom severity and prevalence profiles.
Women with CFS had diminished heart rate and blood pressure responses to cognitive stress, not worsened by prior maximal exercise; lowest reactivity tracked with higher symptom severity.
Serum IgE did not differ between CFS (133 IU/mL) and controls (128), including after stratifying by allergy skin test and rhinitis type.
note: Null result; argues against IgE/mast cell role

finding: Latent profile analysis gave two subclasses (68% and 32%, the latter more somatoform) with large between-centre variation.
SF-36 scores were two to three SD below normal on six subscales in CFS patients, similar across countries.
Adolescents with CFS had elevated somatic complaints and school absence; only 4 of 15 had an Axis I psychiatric diagnosis.
Development of a four-scale Family Response Questionnaire for relatives of people with CFS.
ACTH responses to hCRH, insulin stress and D-fenfluramine were intact, but cortisol responses were lower once ACTH was controlled, and 24-h urinary free cortisol was lower in CFS.
After a 12-week walking programme, SCL-90-R distress scores fell and symptoms did not worsen.
Hypothesis that elevated nitric oxide/peroxynitrite underlies CFS, fibromyalgia, MCS and PTSD overlap.
CFS patients had gait abnormalities versus sedentary controls but postural sway was normal and gait differences were not worsened by light exercise.
Veterinary 'CFS' with staphylococcal blood cultures in dogs and cats.
CFS patients had about 1.7-2.3 times more GP consultations than matched controls in each of the 15 years before onset.
note: Authors read as behavioural; prodromal illness is an alternative explanation

finding: Baseline plasma leptin was not different from controls; 28 days of hydrocortisone (10 mg) raised leptin versus placebo in a randomized crossover.

n: 114 CFS, 125 FM vs healthy and disease controls
finding: Autoantibodies to a 68/48 kDa nuclear protein were found in 13.2% of CFS (and 15.6% of primary FM) but no healthy controls.
Two-thirds of CFS clinic patients were dissatisfied with medical care, mostly over diagnostic delay and perceived dismissiveness.
HLA class I and II frequencies did not differ between CFS patients and controls.
Tilt discriminant score was high in CFS (3.72) but not in fibromyalgia (-3.68) or healthy controls (-4.62), indicating different homeostatic responses.
note: Same group as other HIS studies

finding: Resting HMPAO-SPECT showed no difference in rCBF abnormalities between CFS twins and healthy co-twins, with or without adjustment for fitness and depression.
Over 10 weekly sessions CFS patients were slower but not less accurate, and showed greater intraindividual variability than controls.
13 years after onset, 37% of 35 considered themselves resolved, 43% well but not resolved, 11% chronically ill, 9% worse.
Neural-network classifiers on 29 immune factors found decreased CD19+ B cells and CD34+ progenitors and raised IL-4 in CFS, suggesting a type 2 shift not seen with linear methods.
note: n not in abstract; data-mining, no replication

finding: Interviews showed illness disrupted biography and identity, with partial transformation and some perceived gains.
CFS had higher serum aluminium and lower iron, and women had lower DHEAS, with no difference in cortisol, zinc, copper, ferritin or transferrin.
note: Small; DHEAS lower only in women

finding: mCPP-induced prolactin rise and slow-wave sleep reduction were normal in CFS, while plasma free tryptophan was lower, pointing to presynaptic rather than 5-HT2c receptor changes.
Patent claiming dopamine agonists for fibromyalgia and CFS.
Patent claiming cabergoline-type compounds for fibromyalgia and CFS.
Patent claiming phenylazacycloalkane compounds for fibromyalgia and CFS.
Patent claiming heterocyclic amine compounds for fibromyalgia and CFS.
About half of CFS patients had delayed-type hypersensitivity to Candida antigens, correlating with in vitro T-cell activation and urinary neopterin kinetics.
note: Preliminary, no controls in abstract; near-duplicate of 11933752

finding: 24-h urinary free cortisol was lower in CFS regardless of psychiatric comorbidity, medication use, sleep disturbance or disability.

n: 5 exposed vs two matched CFS subgroups
finding: Five CFS patients with onset after ciguatera or solvent exposure had more severe immune abnormalities (abnormal CD4/CD8, low CD56+ NK in three) than post-EBV or depressed CFS groups.
CFS and depression had distinct cognitive profiles, and CFS-related cognitions predicted disability and fatigue at 6 months.
Descriptive classification of 58 CFS/fibromyalgia web resources.
CFS had lower serum transferrin and higher in vitro LDL/VLDL peroxidation (6630 vs 5581 nmol MDA, p=0.035) than fatigued non-CFS patients.
note: Comparison group was fatigued non-CFS, not healthy

finding: CFS patients had working-memory deficits only on demanding tasks needing resistance to interference and switching.
86% of adolescent girls with CFS reported premorbid problems; psychosocial adjustment was largely normal versus norms.
48-h core body temperature rhythm differed between CFS and controls only in third-harmonic phase angle (p=0.02).
Brain MRI abnormalities were associated with lower SF-36 physical functioning (rho=-0.31, p=0.03) in CFS.
note: No control group; abnormalities were nonspecific white matter findings

finding: CFS patients had delayed orthostatic hypotension and reduced foot-vein contractile compliance to norepinephrine, implying impaired venous sympathetic innervation and leg venous pooling.

population: CFS-like illness in British Gulf War veterans
finding: CFS prevalence was 2.1% in Gulf, 0.7% in Bosnia and 1.8% in Era veterans; MCS was 1.3%, 0.3% and 0.2%, with pesticide exposure strongly linked to MCS.
Onset month was non-random, with excess January onsets in CFS and idiopathic chronic fatigue.
PBMC from CFS patients showed greater in vitro suppression by dexamethasone (37% vs 17%) with normal glucocorticoid receptor number and affinity.
Patent for HHV-6 transfer factors for CFS and MS.
Patent for bovine HHV-6 transfer factor product for CFS and MS.
Illness perceptions (consequences, identity) explained 15% of fatigue, 28% of depression and 30% of anxiety variance in a CFS clinic sample.
Vasopressin infusion produced a reduced ACTH response and a faster cortisol rise in CFS, interpreted as reduced hypothalamic CRH secretion.
Basal hormones were normal, but ACTH, epinephrine, prolactin and TSH responses 4 min after maximal treadmill exercise were lower in CFS, with no group differences the next day.
note: Sedentary matched controls; n not in abstract

finding: Corticospinal MEP threshold and latency were normal in CFS despite slower reaction and movement times.
Illness name (CFS vs myalgic encephalopathy vs Florence Nightingale disease) shifted attributions about cause and seriousness.
CFS patients showed a selective deficit on three divided-attention measures with normal intelligence, fluency and memory.
Lateral ventricular volume was larger in CFS, approaching but not reaching statistical significance.
CFS differed from controls in memory, language and spatial domains, and memory deficits persisted after covarying for depression.
CFS patients and their relatives made more somatic attributions for CFS symptoms than controls.
Review and model proposing chronic lymphocyte overactivation, altered Th1/Th2 cytokine ratio and psychological stress sustaining CFS.
Interviews explored how diagnosis shapes identity in people with CFS.
19% of disease-free cancer patients were severely fatigued, comparable to CFS on the Checklist Individual Strength.
4-hourly sampling over 24 h showed preserved circadian rhythms but lower ACTH at 24:00 and 04:00 (p<0.001) and higher prolactin at 04:00 in CFS.

n: 95 patients vs RA/MS and healthy controls
finding: CFS/FM patients reported more emotional neglect and physical abuse than RA/MS patients and healthy controls.
Observation of UK CFS clinic consultations showed conflicting patient and clinician models of the illness.
After exhaustive cycling, CFS twins showed no greater cognitive decline than healthy co-twins, though baseline performance was slightly lower.
note: Cognition tested soon after exercise only; not a PEM time course

finding: Mucosal dryness was reported by 52% of CFS patients and 32% had salivary gland biopsy, Schirmer and symptom findings consistent with primary Sjogren's syndrome.
At about 42 months follow-up, attention, mood, fatigue and disability improved modestly, but most remained functionally impaired and unemployed.
Maximal-exercise fitness (workload vs heart-rate slope) did not differ between CFS patients and matched neighbourhood controls.
note: Authors conclude deconditioning is not a perpetuating factor

finding: Thesis describing a case series and randomised trial of psychological treatment (no abstract available).
Cluster analysis of the Fennell Phase Inventory matched predicted adaptation phases with differences in disability and coping.
Isoproterenol tilt was positive in 19% of CFS twins and 19% of healthy co-twins (matched OR 1.0, 95% CI 0.2-5.4), not supporting a major role for neurally mediated hypotension.
note: Co-twin design; contrasts with unmatched-control studies

finding: Low-dose ACTH raised DHEA equally in CFS and controls, but the DHEA/cortisol ratio fell only in controls.
Female CFS patients reached roughly half the maximal workload and VO2 of matched sedentary controls, with higher resting but lower maximal heart rate.
note: Large cohort, n not in abstract; findings held in maximal-effort subgroup

finding: CFS patients tapped more slowly, had higher TMS motor thresholds, and lacked the normal post-exercise MEP facilitation seen in controls.
Hippocampal volume was normal but right hippocampal N-acetylaspartate was reduced (p=0.005) on 1H-MRS.
Actigraphy over 12 days showed shorter, less intense activity peaks and longer rest in CFS, with about a quarter 'pervasively passive'.
Current psychiatric disorders (mainly depression) were common in fatiguing illness, but CFS and non-CFS subjects did not differ in rates.
Nocturnal salivary melatonin was higher in adolescent CFS at midnight to 02:00 (p<0.001) with unchanged timing; all patients reported unrefreshing sleep.
note: Small; authors advise against melatonin supplementation

finding: Symptom reporting fluctuated over 24 months in 74 community CFS cases, with few symptoms differing by onset type.
During capnography tilt, CFS patients had lower systolic and diastolic BP and lower end-tidal CO2 and higher HR and respiratory rate than controls.
note: Same group as other HIS studies

finding: Adolescents with CFS had more depression and school absence (mean 40 days); JRA parents scored lower on illness-behaviour encouragement.
Gulf War illness patients showed coagulation cascade and platelet activation markers consistent with a hypercoagulable state.
note: Gulf War illness, not ME/CFS; n not in abstract

finding: In community CFS, 40.6% met MCS criteria and 15.6% fibromyalgia criteria; comorbidity added to fatigue severity and disability.
CFS patients were physically weaker with reduced exercise capacity and higher perceived effort than sedentary controls, but were equally unfit.
In a Chicago community sample, women, minorities and non-working people with CFS reported greater disability and symptom severity.
Community CFS cases were subclassified by duration, onset type and preceding stress, with differences in symptoms and disability; medical utilisation and occupation examined.
Patients described extreme exhaustion, weakness, pain, cognitive and sensory problems as the main symptoms.
Influenza vaccination in CFS was safe and produced an antibody response comparable to healthy volunteers, without worsening the illness course.

n: 22 POTS, 14 CFS vs 10 healthy and 20 simple faint
finding: Adolescents with CFS or POTS had lower R-R interval and heart rate variability, raised low-frequency BP variability and attenuated vagal baroreflex transfer.
note: CFS patients selected for orthostatic tachycardia

finding: HHV-6A/B and HHV-7 serology, culture and PCR did not differ between CFS patients and matched controls.
Women with CFS described disruption of relationships, careers and self-perception, with elevated stress measures.
Total, free and acyl carnitine and 20 carnitine esters did not differ between female CFS patients and matched controls.
GH response to insulin hypoglycaemia (peak 17.0 vs 22.1 ug/l, p=0.01) and nocturnal GH secretion were lower in CFS, while arginine and clonidine GH responses did not differ.
note: Atlas notes conflicting GH/IGF reports; this is a large reduction finding

finding: Labial salivary glands in 11 CFS patients showed ductal and acinar changes and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates; only mast cell number differed significantly (Fisher p=0.0125).
A larger share of CFS than MS patients (30% vs 13%) showed reduced effort on a forced-choice memory test, while conventional test impairment was similar (16-17%).
Patent claiming racemic reboxetine for CFS, fibromyalgia and other conditions.
Patent claiming (S,S)-reboxetine for CFS.
Resting SPECT showed increased perfusion in right thalamus, pallidum, putamen and left thalamus in CFS, similar to but not identical with depression.
68% of 31 patients previously given a psychiatric diagnosis had been misdiagnosed, while 35% of those without one had a treatable disorder.
CFS patients scored higher on perfectionism and lower on self-esteem than controls.
Fatigued twins used more avoidance coping than their non-fatigued co-twins.
note: Twin pairs, n not in abstract

finding: Follicular-phase FSH, LH pulsatility, estradiol and progesterone did not differ from controls in CFS or fibromyalgia.
Review concluding herpesvirus evidence in CFS is inconsistent and non-specific, without increased viral detection versus controls.
Hypothesis that enzyme deficiencies could explain CFS and patients should be screened for them.
Solicitous partner responses were associated with greater fatigue severity and pain, especially in satisfying relationships.
HHV-6 IgM was found in 57.1% of CFS vs 16% of healthy donors, and 54% of CFS had antibody to early protein p41/38 vs 8%.
note: Single lab; HHV-6, not EBV; contradicted by case-control 10913395

finding: Patent for RNase L fragment ratio as CFS diagnostic.
Patent claiming tianeptine for neurodegenerative conditions and CFS.
Most patients reported both physical and psychosocial causes of illness; 61% cited chemical imbalance and 51% a virus.
At mean 45.5 months, two-thirds of 25 severely affected children had recovered; recovery was linked to physical illness triggers and higher socioeconomic status.
Adolescents with a CFS history had more personality difficulty or disorder than controls.
91% of CFS twins and 71% of co-twins had used alternative treatments, with CFS twins using many more.
CFS patients performed worse than healthy controls on cognitive tests but better than depressed patients, and had marked motor impairment similar to MDD.

Dexamethasone had a reduced maximal effect on T-cell proliferation, terbutaline's regulation of TNF-alpha and IL-10 was reduced, and baseline adrenaline was higher in CFS; baseline and CRH-induced cortisol and ACTH were unchanged.
A 37 kDa 2-5A binding polypeptide was found in 88% of CFS patients vs 28% of controls, and in 11% of healthy subjects.
Borrelia-seropositive recruits without clinical Lyme disease reported more chronic fatigue (p=0.02) and malaise (p=0.01) than seronegative recruits.
Thesis testing a cognitive-behavioural model of low self-esteem, attributions and defensive coping in CFS.
Short hypothesis that free radicals underlie morphological and biochemical changes in CFS, by analogy with rheumatoid arthritis.
Systematic review of randomised trials of CBT versus usual care or other interventions in adult CFS (results not visible in the abstract).

n: 258 long vs 28 short duration vs 79 controls
finding: Long-duration CFS (median 18 years) had more severe cognitive difficulties than short-duration CFS in a postal questionnaire.
Hypothesis that sustained peroxynitrite elevation after infection causes CFS and lowers HPA activity.
Sociological account of how people with CFS seek legitimacy and become lay experts.
Sudden-onset CFS began non-randomly across the year, peaking November to January.
Polysomnography found sleep apnea/hypopnea (AHI>=5) in 46% and objective sleepiness (MSLT<10 min) in 30%, with no association to CFS symptom scales.
Hypothesis that abnormal ion channel function underlies fluctuating CFS symptoms.
71% of 35 CFS patients met criteria for a current psychiatric disorder, 54% for depressive disorder.
31% of Australian GPs did not believe CFS is a distinct syndrome; counselling was the most common treatment.
Patients with CFS, FM or TMD met lifetime criteria for IBS, MCS, headache and each other's diagnoses more often than healthy controls.
note: Symptom checklist; n not in abstract

finding: CFS had higher malondialdehyde (p<0.006), methaemoglobin (p<0.02) and 2,3-DPG (p<0.04), with methaemoglobin associated with symptom expression.
note: Small; very high R-squared suggests overfitting

population: ME/CFS (1988 CDC) and fibromyalgia, general population
n: 74 FMS vs 32 widespread pain vs 23 localized pain
finding: In a population survey, 58% of women and 80% of men with fibromyalgia also met 1988 CDC CFS criteria, versus 26% and 22% in widespread pain controls.
Most cardiovascular reflex tests did not differ, but heart rate response to mental arithmetic was lower in CFS (22.6 vs 29.5 beats, p<0.05) and Valsalva BP responses were larger.
Telephone interviews found men and women experienced CFS similarly but were treated differently by medical practitioners.
Half of adolescents with a history of CFS had psychiatric disorders (mainly anxiety), more than controls, more often among those who had recovered.
Night-time plasma melatonin was higher in women with fibromyalgia than controls; authors found no rationale for melatonin replacement in FM or CFS.
Development and validation of the 13-item Chronic Fatigue Attitudes Test.
Dutch GPs recognised CFS in 112 per 100,000 (fibromyalgia 157), a minimum estimate.
CFS without psychiatric history had more small frontal subcortical white-matter hyperintensities on T2 MRI, but combined CFS vs controls did not differ significantly.
In 91 mycoplasma-positive CFS/FM patients, M. pneumoniae (54), M. fermentans (44), M. hominis (28) and M. penetrans (18) were detected, with multiple infections in 48.
CFS and MS groups both had higher harm avoidance and lower reward dependence than healthy controls.
Only 12% reported recovery after about nine years; better baseline function and lower anxiety predicted recovery.
Cortisol responses to a 1 ug Synacthen test did not differ from controls, giving no support for low adrenal reserve.
note: Low responses overall in both groups

finding: CFS patients had slower reaction times and reduced premovement readiness potentials, but normal N100 and P300 potentials.
Resting alpha2-macroglobulin was 29% higher in CFS (p<0.008) and IL-6 secretion about 38% higher (p=0.035 on repeated measures), with higher perceived exertion after 15 min of stepping exercise.
During a sustained 20% elbow-flexion contraction, endurance was shorter in CFS (13.1 vs 18.6 min) with TMS changes consistent with reduced central motor drive and higher perceived effort.
CFS and RA patients did not differ on perfectionism, defensiveness or attitudes to mental illness; social adjustment was poorer in CFS.
CFS point prevalence was 0.42% (95% CI 0.29-0.56) in a Chicago community sample, highest in women, minority groups and lower-education groups.
VO2peak was predicted by peak work rate (r2=0.88), VO2 per unit workload was normal, and a single maximal test caused no lasting deterioration.
note: Assessed only after single test; no PEM measures

finding: CFS showed reduced information-processing speed and efficiency with intact phasic arousal and visual selective attention; verbal recall deficit reflected poor initial storage.
Borrelia burgdorferi immune complex tests were nonreactive in all CFS patients and controls.
Twelve adolescents with CFS and Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (six classical, six hypermobile) all had postural tachycardia or neurally mediated hypotension.
Adrenal gland bodies on CT were reduced by over 50% in 8 CFS patients with subnormal 1 ug ACTH test response compared with 55 healthy subjects.
Family history reported more cancer, autoimmune disease and CFS-like conditions in parents of CFS patients, with no difference in mental disorders.
No Borna disease virus antibodies (169 patients vs 62 controls) or BDV transcripts (18 severe CFS) were found.
Depression in CFS was not associated with pain, psychophysiological syndromes or unexplained symptoms, only with lower social function.
